description: Ukrainian F-16s have destroyed more than 2,500 one-way attack drones, but repeated interceptions are wearing out the country's small fleet.

title: EU fails to reach deal to lift sanctions on Russian oligarchs
description: EU countries failed Monday to finalise a deal that involved lifting sanctions on Russian oligarchs Alisher Usmanov and Mikhail Fridman, Multiple diplomats said earlier that member states had reached a provisional agreement to take the pair off the EU's blacklist as part of a compromise to extend sanctions on almost 3,000 other individuals and entities over the Ukraine war. France 24's Dave Keating has more from Brussels.

title: Flights cancelled, evacuations urged as Typhoon Dujuan hits Japan
description: More than one million people were under evacuation advisories in Japan early Tuesday and hundreds of flights have been cancelled as Typhoon Dujuan brushed past Tokyo, bringing torrential rains, flooding and landslides to the region.

title: Macron, Trump hold 'constructive' talks ahead of UN General Assembly
description: French President Emmanuel Macron said on Monday he had "very constructive" talks with his US counterpart Donald Trump on the conflicts in the Middle East and Ukraine as they met in New York ahead of the annual gathering of world leaders at the United Nations General Assembly. France 24’s Philip Turle takes a closer look at what came out of Macron and Trump’s bilateral meeting and what to look out for at the UN later today.

title: Live: Guterres to open UN General Assembly for the last time as secretary-general
description: UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres will open the General Assembly in New York on Tuesday for the last time before his term ends on December 31. Guterres will be followed at the podium by Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, US President Donald Trump and French President Emmanuel Macron. Follow our live blog for the latest developments.

title: How to break the negative habit of 'toxic multitasking'?
description: PRESS REVIEW – Tuesday, September 22: The Moscow Times talks about mobilisation rumours scaring anti-war activists in Russia. Next: The New York Times interviews South Korea's President Lee Jae Myung. Also: why is multitasking bad for the brain and the nervous system? Finally: this year's Fat Bear contest is starting in Alaska. Who's going to be the chonkiest chonk?

title: 'Great deal of scepticism' as Trump launches own TV channel
description: The White House launched a "Trump TV" stream on Monday evening, days after Trump banned three media outlets from the White House. The White House said the stream will run videos and highlights of what it calls the Trump administration's achievements but critics have compared it to state propaganda networks seen in autocratic countries such as North Korea, reports the Guardian’s Washington bureau chief David Smith.

title: First New York, now Berlin: Why the left turn for major metropolises?
description: There's the inroads of the far right, but also the broader desire for change. Introducing Berlin's answer to Zohran Mamdani: Elif Eralp, who led the far-left Die Linke party's historic win in Sunday's municipal elections in Berlin. We ask if the 45-year-old daughter of Turkish political exiles can push through her promises of rent freezes and nationalisation of private real estate companies. title: UK to offer Saudi Arabia aerial refueling to counter Houthi attacks
description: A British tanker plane will provide "defensive" air-to-air refuelling for Saudi warplanes to help the country defend against Houthi strikes, the UK government confirmed late Monday. The show of solidarity follows a Saudi request for military support after the Houthis increased drone and missile attacks on it in recent weeks alongside a lightning offensive to capture Yemen's Red Sea coast.

title: ‘Hope’ rises in Berlin immigrant communities as Left wins amid AfD gains
description: The Left party, led by Turkish-origin Elif Eralp, won Berlin, offering a contrast to the far rights wins in the east.

title: Iran’s Pezeshkian meets Pakistan’s Naqvi in Tehran as tensions with US rise
description: Pakistani interior ministers trip to Tehran is his sixth and comes as Islamabad, Doha seek to revive diplomacy with US.

title: Palestinians turn to communal ovens to bake bread in Gaza
description: Amid Gaza’s food crisis, bread remains a staple as displaced families use communal ovens to save on costly fuel.

title: To Kill A Mockingbird first edition found in London charity shop
description: An original US edition of To Kill a Mockingbird is found in an Oxfam store in west London.
